Ryan (CTO): Thanks for joining the runtime section of the all-hands. I'm starting this thread for follow-ups and Qs specifically about performance, batching, caching, and kernel work. Drop questions and I'll loop in folks.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Quick note — we'll share the kernel perf slides after sync. If you're asking about batching thresholds, say whether it's latency-sensitive or throughput-first.
Mike C (Infra): For Dedicated customers, are we still planning to expose route-level batching config? Will this be in Console or YAML? @Ana (Product)
Ana (Product): Yes, plan is Console + API. We'll ship CLI iteration first then Console controls behind feature flag. Targeting EOY for GA.
Jules (EngOps): Question — can we get more details on dynamic batching fallbacks? e.g., if KV cache hit rate drops, do we drop batch size or switch to lower-quant model?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Good one. Current plan: prefer reducing batch inter-arrival wait (lower latency) for latency-SLO customers, otherwise autoshrink the batch size when queue length drops. Model fallback to lower-quant variant is a separate policy and only used under capacity pressure.
Ryan (CTO): Also to clarify: fallbacks are policy-driven. We have three tiers: (1) intra-pool kernel swap (fast), (2) model variant fallback (quantized), (3) regional fallback. We'll publish a decision matrix.
Anonymous: Any timeline for kernel work around attention optimizations for long contexts? We saw big gains in the demo.
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Long-context kernels are on the roadmap. Prototype landed in feature branch — aiming for limited internal deploy in 3 weeks, public beta in ~8 weeks. Main risk: fragmentation of kernel matrix across GPUs.
Mike C (Infra): On that fragmentation note: we're prototyping a "kernel affinity" scheduler that keeps similar seq-len work on same pool to reduce kernel thrash. Hoping this reduces memcpy/compilation overhead.
Ana (Product): For customers worried about cost, will Optimize auto-recommend quantized variants? And how will we surface quality regressions?
Sophie (Runtime Eng): Optimize will recommend quant/kv caching. Quality regressions will be linked to eval prompt sets and surfaced in Console with diffed outputs. We'll gate auto-switching with a canary rollout.
Jules (EngOps): Action item: Sophie to post a short doc with fallback matrix + knobs; Mike to share kernel-affinity prototype notes; Ana to confirm Console flag roadmap. I'll add to the follow-up tracker.
atlas-bot: Note added to follow-up tracker: "runtime-fallbacks-kernels" by Jules.
Ryan (CTO): Thanks — if others have Qs paste here. We'll turn this into a short FAQ and link in the all-hands notes. :thumbsup:
